title: Variable
description: One variable in one release, as the publisher documents it. One per line in metadata/releases/<release>/variables.jsonl. Corrections are not applied here; they live in corrections.jsonl. See STANDARD.md §4.

table.description: The table this variable belongs to; required when the release declares tables.

label.description: The publisher's short label or description, verbatim.

description.description: The publisher's definition or description of the variable, verbatim. For data without questions (administrative, census) this is the main text.

questions.description: Question text, verbatim. Usually one entry. Several entries when the wording differs by wave, form or mode (e.g. ANES VCF0803); each then says where it applies.

storage_type.description: How the value is stored in the data file.

measure.description: What kind of quantity the valid values are. Descriptive, not an analysis decision.

variable_type.description: How the variable was produced, when the publisher says. response: a direct answer or observation. recode: recoded from one other variable. computed: derived from several. imputation_flag: flags imputed values. weight and design: survey weights and design variables. administrative: paradata or records added by the publisher.

values.description: Every documented code, valid and missing, in the publisher's order.

valid_range.description: For numeric variables whose valid values are not all labeled (thermometers, ages, counts). Labeled codes inside the range still appear in values.

universe.description: Who was asked, verbatim from the publisher when available.

availability.description: Where the variable has data: one entry per (wave, form, sample, mode) combination the publisher documents. An entry with only wave means everyone in that wave.

notes.description: The publisher's notes on this variable, verbatim.

source_location.description: Where a person can read this variable's documentation.

upstream_id.description: The publisher's or upstream package's own id for the variable, e.g. NORC's variable number.

provenance.description: Where the fields came from. 'record' applies to every field unless 'fields' overrides it.

codes.description: The default origin for this record's missing and unresolved codes. A code without its own origin takes this one; pdt check requires one or the other.

text.description: The full text as the publisher gives it, including stem and interviewer instructions if they aren't separated.

stem.description: Text shared by every item in a battery, when the publisher separates it.

item.description: The text specific to this item, when the publisher separates it.

instructions.description: Interviewer or show-card instructions, when the publisher separates them.

waves.description: Waves this wording applies to. Omit when it applies to all.

condition.description: When this wording is used, in the publisher's words, e.g. a skip condition ("IF R IS MARRIED").

kind.description: valid or missing, as the sources say. unresolved: the sources don't say whether, or why, this code is missing. Record that rather than guess; origin.note says what was checked.

n.description: Cases with this code in the release, as the publisher's codebook prints it. 0 means a code listed with no cases; leave it out when the publisher prints no count. Lets a comparison of releases tell a code with no cases from a new code.

origin.description: Where the kind and missing types came from. Missing and unresolved codes need an origin, their own or the record's provenance.codes (checked by pdt check).

form.description: Questionnaire form, ballot or version (GSS ballot A, MTF form 3).

sample.description: Subsample, e.g. a panel or a cross-section.

n.description: Number of non-missing responses, when known.
